title: Maneuvering
coreMove: Turn detours, timing, signals, and restraint into advantage without exhausting the force that has to arrive.
sourcePressure: The source warns that maneuvering is difficult, weighs forced marches of a hundred, fifty, and thirty li, insists on local guides, signals, mood, strength husbanding, and leaving an outlet for a surrounded foe.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating maneuver as simply moving fast or outworking the opponent.

sourceAnchors.name: gongs and drums, banners and flags
sourceAnchors.detail: The Book of Army Management is cited for using sound and sight to focus a large host where ordinary words and objects fail.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: When the group is too large for speech, design the signal before you blame the group.

sourceAnchors.name: the hundred li forced march
sourceAnchors.detail: Forced marching a fully equipped army a hundred li for advantage leaves leaders captured and only a tenth arriving.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: An advantage that arrives with one-tenth of your strength is not an advantage.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle
examples: manager staring at a spreadsheet with a coffee cup

tryThisNowSpec: Before rushing a team toward an opening, identify what must arrive with them: information, supplies, authority, and the signal everyone will follow.
